1mkb4me:252: : The article's deepest insight is the cascading impact of thermal throttling on the GPU fabric network. When a single GPU downclocks due to high temperature, its data consumption rate drops, causing Priority Flow Control (PFC) in RDMA/RoCE networks to trigger micro-stalls. These stalls propagate through the fabric, affecting data transfers on neighboring nodes and forming a cascade effect similar to traffic jams. In a 1024-node cluster, thermal instability on a single node can reduce the throughput of the entire training job by 10-15%. This coupling of heat, network, and compute is the hidden value of liquid cooling—it not only solves the heat dissipation problem but also eliminates the root cause of network congestion.

1xpanfr:243: : The core difference between liquid cooling and air cooling lies not only in per-GPU temperature control, but also in the cluster-level performance amplification effect. SuperMicro research shows that under full load, DVFS on air-cooled GPUs reduces the clock frequency to 75-80% of nominal, meaning a 5000-GPU air-cooled cluster has an actual compute capacity equivalent to only 3750-4000 full-frequency GPUs. Liquid cooling, however, can maintain 97-99% FLOPs availability, allowing a 4000-GPU liquid-cooled cluster to match or even surpass the performance of a 5000-GPU air-cooled cluster. This is not a linear difference—the larger the cluster, the more pronounced the advantage of liquid cooling.
